name: alias
description: Creates command shortcuts: a short name that expands to a longer command.

flags.description: Bypass an alias once (\ls runs real ls).

examples.explanation: Now ll shows a detailed listing with file-type indicators.
Makes grep highlight matches by default — a popular quality-of-life alias.
Two dots jump up one directory.
Lists everything currently aliased, including distribution defaults like ll and la.

about: Aliases are shell-only (not available in scripts by default) and live per-session unless defined in ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc. For anything parameterized or scriptable, prefer a shell function instead of an alias.
mistakes: Defining aliases in a script and expecting them to exist — scripts need functions or full paths.
Alias shadowing a real command and then confusion in scripts that run on other machines.
warnings: Aliasing rm to rm -i trains habits that fail on servers without the alias. Prefer awareness over safety aliases.
